PyFixest 0.70 moves the state of a fitted model out of loose private attributes
such as `fit._se`, `fit._vcov`, or `fit._X` into typed components: `fit.model`,
`fit.options`, `fit.sample_info`, `fit.coeftable`, `fit.variance_covariance`,
`fit.fitstat`, `fit.sandwich`, `fit.first_stage`, and others. Each component is
documented in the [API reference](/reference/index.qmd).

The compatibility layer preserves the names listed below while you migrate:

- Most listed names are **deprecated aliases**. They reconstruct the former
  representation from the current fit and emit a `PyfixestDeprecationWarning`
  that names the replacement. They do not rerun the 0.60 estimator.
- Some 0.60 representations are no longer supported. Their names are **removed**:
  reading them raises an `AttributeError` that explains why and names the
  replacement.
- On weighted OLS and IV fits, `fit._u_hat` includes the square-root observation
  weights, as in 0.60. Use `fit.resid()` for residuals in the outcome's units.

Internal solver caches and other names outside this table are not covered by
the compatibility layer. An alias also raises `AttributeError` if the required
state was discarded by `lean=True` or has not been computed yet.

```{python}
import warnings

import pyfixest as pf
from pyfixest.errors import PyfixestDeprecationWarning

data = pf.get_data()
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    old = fit._se

print(caught[0].message)
print((old == fit.coeftable.se).all())
```

## Find the old names in your code

`PyfixestDeprecationWarning` is a `FutureWarning`, so Python shows it by
default. To find reads of aliases whose warnings are enabled, turn the
warning into an error, for example in your test suite:

```{python}
#| eval: false
warnings.simplefilter("error", PyfixestDeprecationWarning)
```

With pytest, add `"error::pyfixest.errors.PyfixestDeprecationWarning"` to the
`filterwarnings` setting instead.

## Values that differ from the new components

The aliases reconstruct the former values where possible. The following
conventions and explicit exceptions matter when moving to the new field named
in the warning and in the "Use instead" column:

- **Weighted arrays.** PyFixest 0.60 stored the arrays of weighted OLS and IV
  fits multiplied by the square root of the weights (`_Y`, `_X`, `_Z`,
  `_u_hat`, `_X_hat`, `_v_hat`, `_sumFE`), and the final IRLS arrays of GLMs multiplied
  by the square root of the working weights (`_Y`, `_X`, `_Z`, `_u_hat`, and
  `_sumFE` of weighted fits). The aliases apply the same scaling. The new components hold the unweighted
  arrays: `fit.within_data`, `fit.working_state`, `fit.first_stage`, and
  `fit.fixef_estimates`.
  Fixed-effects-only OLS retains the former column shape of `_u_hat` and
  returns `None` for `_Z`; `fit.resid()` always returns a flat array.
- **Estimation changes.** Aliases reflect the numerical changes described in
  the [0.70 changelog](/changelog.qmd): weighted
  RMSE divides by the sum of weights; Gaussian GLMs now publish R² measures
  and RMSE and use t-based coefficient inference; and changes to IRLS can
  change Poisson, logit, and probit results slightly.
- **Empty defaults.** PyFixest 0.60 set many attributes to an empty array,
  `None`, or `NaN`. An alias raises `AttributeError` when its component is
  absent, for example `fit._sumFE` before `fit.fixef()` runs or `fit._eff_F`
  before `fit.IV_Diag()` runs. Some components are never published for a
  particular fit: FE-only fits have no coefficient inference (`_se`, `_vcov`,
  `_vcov_type`, `_G`), and fits other than saturated event studies have no
  event-study design (`_yname`, `_att`, and the other design names).
  On unsplit fits `_sample_split_value` also raises instead of returning the
  old `all` marker. On full-sample `fsplit` fits it returns the string `"all"`
  so table packages retain the sample label.
- **Fixed-effect coefficients.** `_alpha` raises an error because its positional
  layout changed, including the handling of unused categorical levels. Use
  `fit.fixef()` for a table labelled by fixed-effect term and level, or
  `fit.fixef_estimates.fixed_effects` after calling `fixef()` for the coefficient
  records. The new `fit.fixef_estimates.alpha` uses the current dummy layout and
  is not a substitute for the old array's positional indexing.
- **Sample metadata.** `_k_fe` is removed: its encoded pandas Series labels and
  process-dependent ordering are no longer supported. Use
  `fit.fixef_counts.n_levels_by_fe` for the level counts in the final estimation
  sample, in the order of `fit.model.fixed_effects`.
  `_n_fe` returns the number of fixed effects. After Poisson separation, it
  counts only fixed effects with more than one remaining level, as in 0.60.
  After separation, 0.60's
  `_na_index` omitted the separated rows; that set cannot be rebuilt, so the
  alias raises an informative error. Use `fit.sample_info.dropped_row_index`
  for rows removed by all filtering stages. Non-Poisson GLMs' `_N_rows`
  includes the separated rows, as in 0.60; use
  `fit.sample_info.n_rows` for the fitted row count.
- **Lists instead of tuples.** `_icovars` and `_clustervar` return a list or
  `None`, `_collin_index` returns an empty list when no column was dropped, and
  `_G` repeats the smallest cluster count three times under the default
  `ssc(G_df="min")`.
- **Canonical formulas.** `_fml` and `_model_name` return the canonical
  formula PyFixest now stores, such as `Y ~ 1 + X1`; `_fixef` joins the fixed
  effects with `+` and no spaces. Interacted fixed effects appear as `f1:f2`
  instead of `f1^f2` in all three names. `FixestFormula` raises an informative
  error because its parsed-formula interface changed; use
  `fit.model.parsed_formula`. `_model_spec` exposes the current formulaic
  specifications, including their current fixed-effect encoding.
- **Changed support.** `_support_crv3_inference` reports that non-Poisson GLMs
  no longer accept CRV3 inference. The other capability aliases likewise
  report current support. There is no `fit.capabilities.iid` field:
  use `fit.vcov(vcov="iid")` to request IID inference, which validates support.
- **DID2S metadata.** `_vcov_type` is now `"CRV"` instead of `"CRV1"`;
  `_clustervar` names the cluster variable and `_is_clustered` is true.
  `_G` now returns a list (padded under `G_df="min"`) instead of the old
  integer count. `_ssc` is a `(1, 1)` array containing `1.0`, rather than the
  old one-dimensional OLS correction: the stored covariance already includes
  the two-step GMM calculation.
- **Methods.** `get_performance()` remains callable with a deprecation
  warning; read the automatically computed `fit.fitstat` instead.
  The former IV `first_stage()` method is now the `fit.first_stage` data
  component and cannot be called. The first stage is fitted automatically;
  read `fit.first_stage.model` and `fit.first_stage.diagnostics`, and use
  `fit.IV_Diag()` for additional diagnostics.

## Names still read by other packages

Released versions of [marginaleffects](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/pymarginaleffects)
and [maketables](https://github.com/py-econometrics/maketables) read some of
these names directly, including maketables' use of `_adj_r2`,
`_sample_split_var`, and `_sample_split_value`. The table marks
these aliases as silent: they are documented as deprecated but do not emit a
runtime warning yet. Once the consuming packages release versions using the
new components and users have had an upgrade window, a later PyFixest release
can enable warnings. Removal follows a warning period; publishing an upstream
fix does not immediately remove an alias. No removal version is scheduled yet.

## All deprecated names

"Model classes" names the classes whose fits the row applies to; subclasses
follow their parent, so a `Feols` row also covers IV, GLM, and quantile fits
unless a later row names them.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pyfixest.estimation.models._deprecated_attributes import (
    DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES,
    Removed,
)

print("| Old attribute | Model classes | Use instead | Status |")
print("|---|---|---|---|")
for attribute in DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES:
    for class_name, entry in attribute.classes.items():
        if isinstance(entry, Removed):
            status = f"Removed: {entry.reason}"
        else:
            status = "Deprecated alias" + (" (silent)" if attribute.silent else "")
        print(
            f"| `fit.{attribute.name}` | `{class_name}` "
            f"| `{entry.replacement}` | {status} |"
        )
```
